title: Cranberry Apricot Almond Granola
changes_from_base: Slow-baked at a low heat for 90 min and stirred often: oats, flaked almonds, chia and milk powder are coated in maple syrup, oil, almond butter and almond flavouring, with cranberries and apricots stirred in once cold.
summary: An almond-based granola enriched with almond butter and studded with tart cranberries and sweet dried apricots, baked low and slow until perfectly dry.
equipment: large rimmed baking tray (about 33 x 46 cm)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan) and line a large rimmed baking tray with baking paper.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix together 356 g rolled oats, 128 g flaked almonds, 82 g chia seeds (or flaxseed) and 21 g skimmed milk powder.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: In a small saucepan or microwave-safe jug, warm 35 g smooth almond butter, ½ tsp almond flavouring, ½ tsp fine salt, 235 ml maple syrup and 110 ml vegetable oil until just warm enough to whisk smooth.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Tip the warm mixture over the dry ingredients and stir thoroughly until everything is evenly moist.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread onto the lined tray and bake for 90 min, stirring thoroughly every 15 min, until golden and completely dry.

steps.title: Add
steps.text: Once cooled, stir through 113 g dried cranberries and 128 g dried apricots diced.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Keep in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months.

tips: Stir the granola thoroughly every 15 minutes to ensure even browning and drying
Make sure the almond butter is well combined with the syrup before pouring, as it can be sticky
Add the dried fruits only after cooling so their moisture doesn't soften the granola
storage: Keep in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
